# celestia-rs

> celestia-rs is an open-source Rust implementation of a Celestia consensus node. One binary runs a consensus full node or validator, an optional data availability (DA) bridge, and a standalone DA light node. It is wire- and consensus-compatible with Go celestia-app and celestia-core, and its DA roles interoperate with Go celestia-node. The project is experimental: expect breaking changes.

This file follows https://llmstxt.org. The Markdown files below are served as plain Markdown. Release binaries run on Apple silicon macOS and on x86-64 or ARM64 Linux.

## When to use celestia-rs

- Run a non-validating Celestia consensus node on Mainnet or Mocha, without a wallet, TIA or stake. Install with `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celestiaorg/celestia-rs/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --channel mainnet`, then `celestia-rs start`.
- Run a consensus node and a DA bridge in one process, instead of `celestia-appd` plus a separate `celestia-node` bridge.
- Bootstrap a node from a state-sync snapshot, or verify application execution against a trusted RPC with `celestia-rs follow`.
- Run a DA light node that samples data availability with `celestia-rs da-light`.
- Migrate a Go `celestia-appd` validator to Rust with Go-compatible keyrings, genesis and `priv_validator_state.json`.
- Compare the Rust and Go nodes: sync time, memory and disk benchmarks, and how many public nodes run each implementation.
- Collect a bug report archive with `celestia-rs debug-bundle`.

Do not use celestia-rs when you need a production-grade, supported node today, or a client library to submit blobs from an application. For those jobs, use the Go celestia-app and celestia-node and their documentation at https://docs.celestia.org.

## Docs

- [Operator website](https://celestiaorg.github.io/celestia-rs/): overview, Mainnet quickstart, benchmarks and operator FAQ
- [Operator website as Markdown](https://celestiaorg.github.io/celestia-rs/index.md): the same overview in Markdown
- [Operator guide](https://celestiaorg.github.io/celestia-rs/operator-guide.md): install, configure, run as a service, validators, DA bridge, ports, pruning and day-to-day operations
- [Hardware](https://celestiaorg.github.io/celestia-rs/hardware.md): hardware targets and pruning assumptions
- [Releasing and release channels](https://celestiaorg.github.io/celestia-rs/releasing.md): how releases move through the Corto, Mocha and Mainnet channels
- [Application modules](https://celestiaorg.github.io/celestia-rs/MODULES.md): which Cosmos SDK and Celestia modules the Rust application implements
- [Benchmarks](https://celestiaorg.github.io/celestia-rs/benchmarks/README.md): Rust and Go sync, memory and disk measurements
- [Security notes](https://celestiaorg.github.io/celestia-rs/security.md): threat model and security review notes

## Data

- [Node census](https://celestiaorg.github.io/celestia-rs/census/): consensus nodes on Mainnet and Mocha by implementation, over time
- [Node census history (JSON)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celestiaorg/celestia-rs/node-census-data/history.json): one summary per crawl
- [Latest Mainnet crawl (JSON)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celestiaorg/celestia-rs/node-census-data/latest/mainnet.json): every node seen in the latest Mainnet crawl
- [Latest Mocha crawl (JSON)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celestiaorg/celestia-rs/node-census-data/latest/mocha.json): every node seen in the latest Mocha crawl
